Today I made my first rigorous and well-informed attempts at heat treating. I'll be damned, but I think it went fairly well in spite of a minor mishap or two, both involving the need for me to obtain some slim re-bar and make some larger tongs.

I treated a couple of chisels I'd likely fouled not knowing to cool them as I used them, so I trimmed up their edges with a file and went at it. The mishaps involved dropping the cutoff chisel twice, once into the quenching bucket (prematurely so it was only annealed) and once back into the forge, where it was headed anyway. The final pull I got it out just below critical heat, eased it butt first into the water with a continuous slow stir, then dropped it and left it when I got straw color just back of the finished edge.

I tested it by making a medium blow on the flat of it against a corner of my anvil piece with the 2.5 lb pein, then did similar with a new chisel; damned if the dents aren't practically identical. I'll bitch about it if I use them later and they fail, I promise :D

Cheers
